matrix.title: CostBench: Evaluating Multi-Turn Cost-Optimal Planning and Adaptation in Dynamic Environments for LLM Tool-Use Agents
matrix.locations: Appendix B.3.1-B.3.2, printed page 12846; main cost-optimal planning evaluation
matrix.problem: Tool planning under flexible costs and dynamic blocking
matrix.method_data: Travel tasks with atomic/composite tools, ground-truth optimal paths and greedy comparison
matrix.metrics: Cost gap, path distances/exact match, task completion, invalid tool use
matrix.overlap: Tool-price sensitivity and cost-aware route choice are already studied
matrix.version_note: arXiv 2511.02734v1 calls the final-candidate metric User Intent Hit Ratio; the ACL PDF calls it Task Completion Ratio. Cite the published name when describing the final paper.
matrix.boundary: Appendix excludes non-goal trajectories from cost/path/completion metrics, and invalid search attempts from the cost calculation; invalid tool-use metric includes all outcomes. Do not characterize the whole paper as ignoring failures.
matrix.difference_hypothesis: We require earlier observable contract drift and later aligned behavior, not final-candidate accuracy as a direct reading of prior intent
matrix.next_action: Report full-cohort completion/failure and all attributable incurred costs; successful-only cost is secondary with its denominator explicit

design_implications.positive_control_role: Admitted revised 728-to-733 would test whether a model can use a genuinely sufficient cache. It does not by itself establish a wrong-task temptation or category C.
design_implications.negative_control_role: Need separately admitted correct-but-insufficient history with a feasible recomputation path. 537-to-555 remains pending, not silently admitted.
design_implications.C_required_observation: A semantically wrong task definition recorded before program/tool selection, followed by a program consistent with that wrong definition. Simultaneous JSON fields or final answer alone do not prove temporal precedence.
design_implications.C_denominator: Keep all preassigned eligible trajectories, including invalid/missing contracts as unresolved or invalid rather than imputing no drift. Report sensitivity bounds if unresolved records affect the endpoint.
design_implications.A_B_boundary: Correct prior contract with unsuitable cache is A; correct prior contract with wrong implementation is B. Without a prior observable definition, A/B/C can be unidentifiable and must remain so.
design_implications.instrumentation: Explicit contract elicitation may protect or alter behavior. Keep it separate from ordinary-workflow error rates and match horizon/information before cross-protocol inference.
design_implications.fairness: Reviewer interpretation and current reference SQL stay with the scorer; do not give only the proposed method the correct contract. Historical public auxiliary evidence must be identical within each contrast.
design_implications.causal_limit: No amount of repeat calls on this one development pair establishes cross-task generalization; available-versus-unavailable post-tool observations may differ through the intervention itself.
design_implications.stopping: If eligible positive controls are used correctly and insufficient caches are rejected without task drift, report that boundary instead of searching model errors by changing task selection or prices.

novelty_claim: Unproven. A potentially sharper measurement target is not yet a novel effective algorithm or a publishable phenomenon.
next_minimal_experiment: No launch until semantic admission and frozen execution plan. Then a small feasibility batch with both sufficient and insufficient history, ordinary outcomes separate from temporally prior elicited contracts, not a confirmatory causal claim.
